primary_claim: Trained per-layer steering vectors (~295K params, ~1/600th the parameter count of the LoRA-based Activation Oracle) can function as an activation oracle on Qwen3-8B, achieving close to standard LoRA Activation Oracle accuracy on the Taboo task, a significant deficit on PersonaQA, and roughly doubled PersonaQA open-ended accuracy (6.8% to 11.5%) when activation collection is 'primed'.

effect.metric: PersonaQA open-ended accuracy improvement from priming activation collection

contradicts_or_qualifies: Surprisingly, the original Activation Oracle paper's LoRA checkpoint achieves 60% accuracy with no activations at all on PersonaQA Y/N, qualifying claims about what drives its performance
PersonaQA Y/N figures here are not directly comparable to the AO paper's reported 69% baseline, likely due to a suspected bug in the Activation Oracles codebase causing non-deterministic N cases
limitations_stated: The vector approach seems more fragile to the specific text activations were collected from than the LoRA approach
quote: Priming nearly doubles Vector AO accuracy (6.8% → 11.5%).
